labels.label: lem:stability

hypotheses.paper: g, g' metrics on Σ (compact, with boundary ⊔ B_j)
hypotheses.note: two FrameMetric (Gram matrices in a measurable frame, positive definite) on one MeasuredModel; vol_g = √det G · μ, bvol_g = √det(Pᵀ G P) · μb_j, |∇u|²_g = du·G⁻¹du are the model's definitions. The passage from a Riemannian manifold to the model waits on T-yamabe-scope.

hypotheses.paper: (1+ε)^{-1} g ≤ g' ≤ (1+ε) g as quadratic forms
hypotheses.note: Comparable ε g g' := ∀ x, QFormComparable (1+ε) (G x) (G' x), the two quadratic-form inequalities at every point; the boundary comparison is derived (QFormComparable.congr), not assumed
stability (product form) holds for every u : D; stability_ratio (printed ratio) assumes F^(β)_g(u) ≠ 0
UniformlyClose η g g': |g'(v,v) − g(v,v)| ≤ η g(v,v) everywhere, η → 0 (tendsto_infF_of_uniformlyClose); tendsto_infF takes any family whose comparability constants tend to 0 (eventually)

findings: Minor (l.699–701): the printed conclusion is a ratio F^(β)_{g'}(u)/F^(β)_g(u), which is 0/0 when F^(β)_g(u) = 0; 'all β_j ≥ 0' allows β = 0, and then u = 1 gives F^(0)_g(1) = 0 (Lean witness Yamabe.toy_F_zero_one). The product form (1+ε)^{-N} F_g ≤ F_{g'} ≤ (1+ε)^N F_g holds for every u (stability). Harmless for the paper: the lemma is used at l.728 with β_j = c_N > 0.
questions: The Riemannian metric is read through a measurable frame (Gram matrix G, frame measures μ, μb_j, boundary frame P). Whether this abstract model is the formalization of record for §6, and how it is instantiated from Mathlib's manifolds, is T-yamabe-scope's ruling; nothing is marked here.

'g' → g uniformly' (l.703) read as uniform convergence in the norm of g itself (sup_x |g' − g|_g → 0), which on a compact manifold is C⁰ convergence of the tensor; the formal statement tendsto_infF_of_uniformlyClose, and the more general tendsto_infF (comparability constants → 0).
inf over W^{1,2}∖{0} read as inf over u with 0 < ‖u‖²_{L^{p*}} < ∞ (Adm); with the Sobolev embedding this is u ≠ 0.

The same finite-energy restriction on D applies to the anchoring of lem:stability's 'consequently' (inf F); stability itself is two-sided, so infinite energies or norms are infinite for both metrics and create no spurious bound.

labels.label: rem:sign

hypotheses.paper: (Σ, g) compact Riemannian N-manifold with boundary ⊔ B_j, N ≥ 3 (l.465, l.605)
hypotheses.note: the abstract MeasuredModel + FrameMetric (see lem:stability); N ≥ 3 carried; compactness carried as IsFiniteMeasure (vol_g), IsFiniteMeasure (bvol_g j); nonemptiness as vol_g ≠ 0 and ∃ j, bvol_g j ≠ 0

hypotheses.paper: g Schwarzschild-like: each (B_j, g) a round sphere of radius r_j (eq:F1-torus, l.467)
hypotheses.note: only Vol(B_j, g) = ω_{N-1} r_j^{N-1} is used (Fq_one_round); constant scalar curvature and minimal boundary are not used by rem:sign's assertions

hypotheses.paper: g of constant scalar curvature, ∂Σ minimal (H_g ≡ 0) (Schwarzschild-like, l.467)
hypotheses.note: not used by any assertion of rem:sign; now also rows of the module's hypothesis checklist

hypotheses.paper: M = −∫ H_ref bvol = ω_{N-1} Σ r_j^{N-2} (l.467)
hypotheses.note: M taken as its round-sphere value roundMass N r; the identity with −∫ H_ref is §4 geometry, not in scope
val φ, tr φ bounded and a.e.-strongly measurable

hypotheses.paper: ∫_Σ φ vol = 0, φ ≤ 0 and φ ≢ 0 on ∂Σ (l.509)
hypotheses.note: ∫ val φ d(vol_g) = 0; tr φ ≤ 0 bvol_j-a.e. for all j; ∃ j, ¬ tr φ =ᵐ[bvol_j] 0

hypotheses.paper: 'Such φ exist (take φ = −1 near ∂Σ and positive in the interior with zero mean)' (l.741)
hypotheses.note: exists_direction builds φ = (∫χ/Vol Σ)·1 − χ from a cutoff χ ∈ D with tr χ = 1 on ∂Σ and ∫χ < Vol(Σ); on a manifold χ is a smooth collar cutoff, whose existence is the manifold-level part (waits on T-yamabe-scope). The toy model exhibits such χ (toy_infF_lt_Fq_one).

findings: eq:hoelder (l.609; not a ledger row, in this target's scope; the curation may attach it to lem:positivity, whose proof uses it at l.720): on any B_j with Vol(B_j) < 1 the constant u = 1 (in W^{1,2}(Σ), trace 1) violates the printed boundary line ‖u‖²_{L²(B_j)} ≤ Vol(B_j)^{2/(N−1)} ‖u‖²_{L^{p♯}(B_j)} (Lean: Yamabe.hoelder_boundary_printed_false_of_lt_one, for every measure of mass in (0,1), e.g. a round B_j of radius r_j < ω_{N−1}^{−1/(N−1)}, r_j < 1/√(4π) for N = 3; and Yamabe.hoelder_boundary_printed_false, a point mass 1/2). The exponent is 1/(N−1) = 1 − 2/p♯ (Yamabe.hoelder_boundary), sharp: equality on constants for every mass (Yamabe.hoelder_boundary_eq_one). Of the two citations of eq:hoelder at l.720 only the second, ‖u_k‖_{L²(B_j)} ≤ Vol(B_j)^{1/(N−1)} ‖u_k‖_{L^{p♯}(B_j)} → 0, uses the boundary line; its factor should be Vol(B_j)^{1/(2(N−1))}, and the step survives since only → 0 is used. The first citation at l.720 ('bounded in W^{1,2}') and l.627 (lem:kobayashi) use the interior line l.607, which is correct (Yamabe.hoelder_interior).
questions: rem:sign's first sentence is stated for the Schwarzschild-like metric (round B_j); formalized with only the areas of the B_j (Fq_one_round, Fq_one_round_three for N = 3: F_g(1) = 4M/Vol^{1/3}, M = Σ 4π r_j).

ω_{N-1} is defined as the total mass of Mathlib's sphere measure volume.toSphere on the unit sphere of ℝ^N (= N·|B^N|, sphereArea_eq), not as a Hausdorff measure; sphereArea_three checks ω_2 = 4π and cN_three checks c_3 = 4√(4π) (eq:cN).
'Theorem thm:upper-bound therefore yields δ > 0 but no size' is commentary and is not formalized; 'inf F_g < F_g(1)' and 'κ < 1' are (infF_lt_Fq_one, kappa_lt_one, assembled in rem_sign).

dirichlet (like normSq) is 0 when infinite. The Riemannian instance (T-yamabe-scope) must take D among finite-energy, finite-norm functions (C^∞(Σ), or W^{1,2}(Σ) by density), where F and inf F are the paper's; an abstract D containing a function of infinite energy or boundary norm would give a Lean inf F below the paper's. Disclosed in the SCOPE of Quotient.lean.

kb_proposals: A real positive definite matrix factors at this pin as A = star R * R via CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self.mp hA.posSemidef.nonneg (needs `open scoped MatrixOrder`); with IsHermitian.mulVec_eigenvectorBasis and det_eq_prod_eigenvalues this proves Loewner-type determinant bounds (Yamabe.det_le), without CFC.sqrt.

Squared real L^q norms are best taken as (eLpNorm f q ν).toReal^2 and compared at the level of measures (eLpNorm_mono_measure, eLpNorm_smul_measure_of_ne_top, withDensity_mono, withDensity_smul'); with a two-sided domination infinite norms are infinite together (Yamabe.toReal_le_of_le_mul), and no measurability is needed.
hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le gets stuck on instances unless (μ := …) (F := …) (F' := …) are named.

A negative first variation gives a strict decrease: by contradiction IsLocalMin.hasDerivAt_eq_zero yields ∃ᶠ ε in 𝓝 0, f ε < f 0; combine with an eventual side condition by Filter.Frequently.and_eventually (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.exists_F_lt_F_one).

lean-yamabe has an abstract measured model of (Σ, ⊔B_j) (YamabeScaffold.Quotient: MeasuredModel, FrameMetric, vol, bvol, gradSq, F) with a two-point witness toyModel/toyMetric (N = 3); later §6 statements can reuse both.
